# Claude Code Documentation Overview

Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool available across terminal, IDE, desktop, and browser. Here's a concise guide to key features:

## Core Features

**What Claude Code Does:**
- Reads and edits your codebase
- Runs commands and integrates with development tools
- Works across multiple platforms and environments
- Operates autonomously through an agentic loop

## Getting Started

1. **[Quickstart](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart.md)** - Setup and first coding session
2. **[Overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview.md)** - Understand capabilities
3. **[How Claude Code Works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works.md)** - Learn the agentic loop and built-in tools

## Key Configuration Files

- **CLAUDE.md** - Persistent project instructions
- **settings.json** - Configuration options
- **.claude/hooks/** - Automation triggers
- **.claude/skills/** - Custom capabilities
- **.claude/subagents/** - Specialized AI agents

## Main Workflows

| Use Case | Documentation |
|----------|---|
| Code review & CI/CD | [Code Review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review.md), [GitHub Actions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions.md) |
| Parallel work | [Agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents.md), [Subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md) |
| Web development | [Chrome integration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome.md) |
| Cloud deployment | [Amazon Bedrock](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock.md), [Google Cloud](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai.md) |

# Extend Claude with skills

> Create, manage, and share skills to extend Claude's capabilities in Claude Code. Includes custom commands and bundled skills.

Skills extend what Claude can do. Create a `SKILL.md` file with instructions, and Claude adds it to its toolkit. Claude uses skills when relevant, or you can invoke one directly with `/skill-name`.

Create a skill when you keep pasting the same instructions, checklist, or multi-step procedure into chat, or when a section of CLAUDE.md has grown into a procedure rather than a fact. Unlike CLAUDE.md content, a skill's body loads only when it's used, so long reference material costs almost nothing until you need it.

<Note>
  For built-in commands like `/help` and `/compact`, and bundled skills like `/debug` and `/code-review`, see the [commands reference](/docs/en/commands).

  **Custom commands have been merged into skills.** A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy` and work the same way. Your existing `.claude/commands/` files keep working. Skills add optional features: a directory for supporting files, frontmatter to [control whether you or Claude invokes them](#control-who-invokes-a-skill), and the ability for Claude to load them automatically when relevant.

# Create Custom Subagents in Claude Code

Subagents are specialized AI assistants that handle specific tasks in isolated context windows. They're ideal for delegating work that would otherwise flood your main conversation with search results, logs, or file contents.

## Quick Start

### Create Your First Subagent

Ask Claude to create a subagent file in `~/.claude/agents/` (user-level, available in all projects) or `.claude/agents/` (project-level):

```text
Create a personal code-improver subagent in ~/.claude/agents/ that scans
files and suggests improvements for readability, performance, and best
practices.
```

Claude generates a markdown file with YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: code-improver
description: Scans files and suggests improvements for readability, performance, and best practices
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: sonnet
---

You are a code improvement specialist. For each issue you find, explain
the problem, show the current code, and provide an improved version.
```

## Key Configuration Fields

| Field | Required | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `name` | Yes | Unique identifier (lowercase, hyphens only) |
| `description` | Yes | When Claude should delegate to this subagent |
| `tools` | No | Allowed tools (inherits all if omitted) |
| `model` | No | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, or full model ID |
| `permissionMode` | No | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `plan`, `bypassPermissions` |
| `skills` | No | Preload skill content into context |
| `memory` | No | Persistent memory scope: `user`, `project`, or `local` |
| `isolation` | No | Set to `worktree` for isolated git worktree |
| `maxTurns` | No | Limit agentic turns before stopping |

## Scope & Location

Store subagents at different locations based on scope:

| Location | Scope | Priority |
|----------|-------|----------|
| Managed settings | Organization-wide | 1 (highest) |
| `--agents` CLI flag | Current session | 2 |
| `.claude/agents/` | Current project | 3 |
| `~/.claude/agents/` | All your projects | 4 |

# How Claude remembers your project

> Give Claude persistent instructions with CLAUDE.md files, and let Claude accumulate learnings automatically with auto memory.

Each Claude Code session begins with a fresh context window. Two mechanisms carry knowledge across sessions:

* **CLAUDE.md files**: instructions you write to give Claude persistent context
* **Auto memory**: notes Claude writes itself based on your corrections and preferences

This page covers how to:

* [Write and organize CLAUDE.md files](#claude-md-files)
* [Scope rules to specific file types](#organize-rules-with-claude/rules/) with `.claude/rules/`
* [Configure auto memory](#auto-memory) so Claude takes notes automatically
* [Troubleshoot](#troubleshoot-memory-issues) when instructions aren't being followed

## CLAUDE.md vs auto memory

Claude Code has two complementary memory systems. Both are loaded at the start of every conversation. Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a [PreToolUse hook](/docs/en/hooks-guide) instead. The more specific and concise your instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them.

|                      | CLAUDE.md files                                   | Auto memory                                                                                      |
| :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Who writes it**    | You                                               | Claude                                                                                           |
| **What it contains** | Instructions and rules                            | Learnings and patterns

# Claude Code Plugins Reference

## Overview

A **plugin** is a self-contained directory that extends Claude Code with custom functionality. Plugins can include skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers, monitors, and themes.

## Plugin Structure

### Standard Layout

```
my-plugin/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json           # Plugin manifest (optional)
├── skills/                   # Skill directories
│   └── my-skill/
│       └── SKILL.md
├── commands/                 # Flat skill files
│   └── status.md
├── agents/                   # Subagent definitions
│   └── reviewer.md
├── hooks/                    # Hook configurations
│   └── hooks.json
├── .mcp.json                # MCP servers
├── .lsp.json                # LSP servers
└── scripts/                 # Supporting scripts
```

## Plugin Manifest (`plugin.json`)

### Required Field

Only `name` is required if you include a manifest:

```json
{
  "name": "my-plugin"
}
```

### Complete Schema Example

```json
{
  "name": "deployment-tools",
  "displayName": "Deployment Tools",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Deployment automation tools",
  "author": {
    "name": "Dev Team",
    "email": "dev@company.com"
  },
  "skills": "./custom/skills/",
  "commands": ["./custom/commands/"],
  "agents": ["./custom/agents/"],
  "hooks": "./config/hooks.json",
  "mcpServers": "./mcp-config.json",
  "lspServers": "./.lsp.json",
  "dependencies": [
    "helper-lib",
    { "name": "secrets-vault", "version": "~2.1.0" }
  ],
  "defaultEnabled": false
}
```

### Key Metadata Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Unique kebab-case identifier for namespacing |
| `displayName` | string | Human-readable name for UI display |
| `version` | string | Semantic version for pinning updates |
| `description` | string | Brief plugin purpose |
| `defaultEnabled` | boolean | Whether plugin loads enabled (default: `true`) |
| `keywords` | array | Discovery tags |
| `metadata` | object | Custom data (not used by Claude

# Claude Code Commands Reference

Commands in Claude Code are invoked with `/` at the start of a message and control the session from within. Here's what you need to know:

## Basic Usage

- **Trigger**: Type `/` to see all available commands, or `/` + letters to filter
- **Syntax**: Commands are only recognized at the message start. Text following the command name becomes its arguments
- **Skills exception**: As of v2.1.199, multiple skills can be chained: `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` (up to 6 skills)

## Command Categories

Commands serve different purposes across your workflow:

### Setup
- `/init` - Generate starter `CLAUDE.md`
- `/memory` - Refine project memory
- `/permissions` - Set approval rules
- `/mcp` - Configure MCP servers

### During Work
- `/model` - Switch AI model
- `/effort` - Adjust reasoning level
- `/plan` - Enter plan mode for large changes
- `/context` - Visualize context usage
- `/compact` - Summarize conversation to free space
- `/btw` - Ask side questions without adding to history

### Code Review & Quality
- `/code-review [level] [--fix]` - Review diff for bugs/cleanup (alias: `/review`)
- `/security-review` - Check for vulnerabilities
- `/diff` - View uncommitted changes interactively

### Parallel Work
- `/tasks` - List background work
- `/background [prompt]` - Detach session as background agent
- `/batch <instruction>` - Decompose large changes across worktrees
- `/fork [prompt]` - Copy conversation to new background session

### Session Management
- `/clear [name]` - Start fresh conversation
- `/resume` - Return to earlier conversation
- `/branch [name]` - Branch to try different direction
- `/rewind` - Roll back code and conversation to checkpoint

### Utilities
- `/copy [N]` - Copy last response to clipboard
- `/export [filename]` - Export conversation as text
- `/goal [condition]` - Set continuous work goal
- `/usage` (alias: `/cost`) - Show token usage
- `/help` - Show available commands

# Claude Code CLI Reference

This is a comprehensive command-line interface reference for Claude Code. Here are the key sections:

## Main CLI Commands

**Starting Sessions:**
- `claude` - Start interactive session
- `claude "query"` - Start with initial prompt
- `claude -p "query"` - Query via SDK and exit
- `cat file | claude -p "query"` - Process piped content

**Session Management:**
- `claude -c` - Continue most recent conversation
- `claude -r "<session>" "query"` - Resume session by ID or name
- `claude --resume` - Show interactive picker for sessions

**Background & Cloud Sessions:**
- `claude --bg "task"` - Start as background agent
- `claude --cloud "task"` - Create web session on claude.ai
- `claude agents` - Monitor and dispatch parallel sessions
- `claude attach <id>` - Attach to background session

**Other Commands:**
- `claude update` - Update to latest version
- `claude auth login/logout/status` - Manage authentication
- `claude doctor` - Print diagnostics
- `claude setup-token` - Generate long-lived OAuth token
- `claude mcp` - Configure Model Context Protocol servers
- `claude plugin` - Manage plugins

## Essential CLI Flags

**Model & Performance:**
```bash
--model claude-sonnet-5      # Set model
--effort high                # Set effort level (low/medium/high/xhigh/max/ultracode)
--advisor opus               # Enable advisor tool
--fallback-model sonnet,haiku # Fallback model chain
```

**Permissions & Security:**
```bash
--permission-mode plan                    # Set permission mode
--dangerously-skip-permissions           # Skip permission prompts
--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions     # Add to mode cycle
--restricted                             # Restricted mode (evaluation/shared machines)
```

**Input/Output & Formatting:**
```bash
--output-format json         # Output format (text/json/stream-json)
--input-format stream-json   # Input format
--json-schema '{"type":"object"}' # Structured output
--verbose                    # Verbose output
```

**Session Configuration:**
```bash
--na
